items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: my father came to me and told me that there was a fellow down the street in the neighborhood that was going to give me piano lessons... His name was Wynberry Boyd... Besides teaching me the fundamentals of the music

ctx.x: was leaving. I was a little puzzled, but I don't... I didn't ask them for what reasons... I don't know why I didn't ask. But I learned later, because I think I communicated with my mother much better than I did my father, that what had happened... The reason for it was that Jack, when he came in, he had been drinking. Just how drunk he was I couldn't have surmised, because he wasn't staggering or anything. But my father must have known that he was pretty drunk. And this smell he had on his breath was the kind he…

Anyway, that was the first and last lesson that I had from Jack Smith. And a couple of weeks later, my father came to me and told me that there was a fellow down the street in the neighborhood that was going to give me piano lessons, which I later learned my father was paying 15 cents a lesson for. So when the proper time came, I went to this fellow. His name was Wynberry Boyd. And since then he's changed his name to Wyn Boyd -- I guess that's for pretty obvious reasons.

But I think this turned out to be another turning point. Because besides teaching me the fundamentals of the music and everything from the characters on the staff and what the time signatures meant, and of course, you always had the do-re-me-fa-sol-la-ti-do in school, and most (?)s were familiar with that...
